title: help
description: What <app> help answers with -o json: the same commands and flags the H-1 layout shows, as data, so a program (hubman, an agent, a test) reads an app's commands without parsing text, and the hidden old forms of renamed commands, marked old (G-STACK-5). mankit's helpout makes it for every app, so every app answers it alike.

kind.description: Always Help, the kind of this answer, so a reader knows which schema its data meets.

data.description: The app's help: what it is, how to start it, its commands and flags, and its old forms.

name.description: The app's command, the first word of every command line, so a reader builds each full form from it.

what.description: One line: what the app is, as the layout's first line says it. Empty when the app says nothing.

start.description: How to start the app and where to run it, one line each, as the layout's Start section. Empty when the app says nothing.

commands.description: The commands people see, the ones the layout lists, in its order: each thing with its own verbs and things, each command that has no thing. A hidden command is left out; an old form is only in old.

flags.description: The app's own flags, those the layout's Flags section lists. Empty when it has none.

more.description: The repository URL, as the layout's More line gives it, so a person finds the source and the docs. Empty when the app names none.

old.description: The hidden old forms of renamed commands, each with the full form it runs: an old form still runs for one release and says the new name on stderr (G-STACK-5). Listed here, and never in the layout, so a reader moves a script to the full form. Empty when there is none.

command.description: One command: a thing, which holds verbs and things of its own, or a verb, which runs.

name.description: The command's own word; its full form is the words of the commands it sits in, then this one.

summary.description: The command's one-line help, as the layout lists it.

usage.description: The command's line as it is typed after the app's name, with its arguments, such as server stop [addr|name], so a reader knows what it takes.

commands.description: A thing's own verbs and things, in the layout's order; empty for a verb.

flags.description: The command's own flags, not those it takes from the commands it sits in. Empty when it has none.

name.description: The flag's long name, without the dashes: --output is output.

shorthand.description: The flag's one-letter form, without the dash, when it has one: -o is o.

type.description: The kind of value it takes, as the flag library names it (bool, string, int, duration, stringSlice …), so a reader knows whether it takes a value.

default.description: The value it has when not given, as text, when that is not the type's zero value.

oldForm.description: One old form of a renamed command and the full form it runs.

words.description: The old words after the app's name, such as servers stop.

now.description: The full form's words after the app's name, such as server stop: the command the old form runs.

args.description: The arguments the old form stands for, given first after the full form's words, when it stood for a verb with an argument: config queue wait runs queue set wait. Left out when it stands for none.
